main.claim: Paste your speech or type a word count, pick a pace, and see how many minutes it will take to say. Normal pace is 130 words per minute; slow is 110 and fast is 160. Free, runs in your browser.

sections.heading: How to turn words into minutes
sections.body:
Paste your speech into the tool, or type the word count if you already know it. Then pick the pace you talk at. The tool shows the speaking time, the word count and the number of pages.

1. Open the [words to minutes tool](https://words-to-minutes.lazur.app/).
2. Paste your text, or type a word count.
3. Pick a pace: slow (110 words per minute), normal (130) or fast (160). Choose custom if you know your own rate.
4. Read the speaking time, the word count and the pages.

**Minutes equal words divided by words per minute.** A 1,300-word talk at 130 words per minute takes 10 minutes. You can do that sum on paper, but the tool does it for you and keeps a table for every length from 1 to 20 minutes.

sections.heading: Pick the pace that matches you
sections.body:
Speakers differ, so the pace matters as much as the word count. Read your script aloud once, the way you would on stage, and time it with a clock. Then divide the words by the minutes you took. If you finished 520 words in 4 minutes, you talk at about 130 words per minute, so pick normal.

If you talk faster than that, pick fast. If you speak slowly and carefully, pick slow. The gap between the presets is wide: a 2,000-word script runs about 15 minutes at normal pace and about 18 minutes at slow. Choose the pace you will really use on the day, not the one you hope for.

sections.heading: Speaking time for common lengths
sections.body:
These numbers come from the same formula the tool uses, at each of its three presets:

- 1 minute: 110 words slow, 130 normal, 160 fast.
- 3 minutes: 330 words slow, 390 normal, 480 fast.
- 5 minutes: 550 words slow, 650 normal, 800 fast.
- 10 minutes: 1,100 words slow, 1,300 normal, 1,600 fast.
- 15 minutes: 1,650 words slow, 1,950 normal, 2,400 fast.

If you have a length in mind, find it in the table, then paste your draft and check that it lands near the number you wanted.

sections.heading: What a word count cannot show
sections.body:
A word count gives you speaking time with no breaks in it. A talk with slides, a pause for questions or a round of applause adds time the count cannot see. Leave a margin for these. Aim to finish a minute or two inside your time limit, then run the speech once with a timer to confirm.

If your script has long names, numbers or lists, read those lines aloud as well. They often take longer to say than the words suggest.

sections.heading: Draft by talking
sections.body: If you draft by speaking, Lazur types what you say into any app on your Mac: hold two keys and talk. Then check the length here before you rehearse, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).

pages.h1: Word count to minutes of speech
pages.claim: A 1,500-word speech takes about 11 minutes and 30 seconds at a normal pace of 130 words per minute. Paste your text or type the count, pick slow, normal or fast, and the tool gives the speaking time. Free, in your browser.

sections.heading: How to get minutes from a word count
sections.body:
Use the tool to turn any word count into speaking time. You can paste the whole script, so the count is exact, or type a number if you only know roughly how long the piece is.

1. Open the [word count to minutes tool](https://words-to-minutes.lazur.app/word-count-speech).
2. Paste your script, or type the word count.
3. Choose a pace: slow (110 words per minute), normal (130) or fast (160). You can also enter a custom rate.
4. Read the speaking time, the word count and the pages.

The formula is simple. Minutes equal words divided by words per minute. For 1,500 words at 130 words per minute, the answer is 11.5 minutes, which is 11 minutes and about 32 seconds. The tool does this sum for you, so you can change the pace and see the new time at once.

sections.heading: Words for common speech lengths
sections.body:
People often ask for a target length, then need the matching word count. At normal pace, these are the counts to aim for:

- 2 minutes: 260 words.
- 7 minutes: 910 words.
- 12 minutes: 1,560 words.

At the slow and fast presets, 12 minutes is 1,320 words or 1,920 words. Paste a draft to see where it falls, then add or cut lines until the speaking time matches the slot you have.

**A 15-minute speech needs about 1,950 words at normal pace.** A script of 1,500 words is short for that slot, and it would finish near 11 and a half minutes.

sections.heading: Choose slow, normal or fast
sections.body:
The three presets are a starting point. Your real pace may sit between them, and a custom rate can match it. To find your own number, read a passage of known length aloud, time it, and divide the words by the minutes.

Slow is useful for a careful, deliberate talk, a eulogy or a script that needs room for emotion. Fast suits a quick pitch or a talk you have given many times. If you are unsure, use normal, rehearse once, and adjust the pace in the tool to match what you heard.

sections.heading: What the count leaves out
sections.body:
The word count gives the speaking time with no breaks. Slides, questions, a pause for a laugh or a slow start with a microphone all add time the count cannot see.

Keep a margin. If the slot is 10 minutes, aim for 9 minutes of speech, then check the real run with a timer. A script with many numbers, names or bullet points often runs longer than the count suggests, so read those parts aloud as you test.

sections.heading: Write the speech by talking
sections.body: If you draft by speaking, Lazur types what you say into any app on your Mac: hold two keys and talk, and the words land where your cursor is. Paste the result here to see how long it will take.

faq.q: How many words is a 5 minute speech?
faq.a: At a normal pace of 130 words per minute, a 5-minute speech is about 650 words. At slow pace (110 words per minute) it is 550 words, and at fast pace (160) it is 800. Paste your own draft to get the exact time.

At normal pace, 700 words take about 5 minutes and 23 seconds, so it runs a little over 5 minutes. At fast pace it takes about 4 minutes and 23 seconds. At slow pace it takes about 6 minutes and 22 seconds.

faq.q: How many words for a 1 minute speech?
faq.a: About 130 words at normal pace. Slow speech fits 110 words in a minute, and fast speech fits 160. Pick the preset that matches how you talk, or enter your own rate in the tool.

faq.q: Is 1500 words enough for a 15 minute speech?
faq.a: No. At normal pace, 1,500 words take about 11 and a half minutes. A 15-minute speech needs about 1,950 words at normal pace, or 1,650 at slow pace. Add content or slow your delivery, then check the new count in the tool.
